rationale: Interpreted the default-configuration reproduction and closed the constructor question's reachability limit. Receipt e0d98aadc54b461792883fc8a2a82676 evaluated all five comparisons with MaxAppendEntries left at its default 64 and a gap of about 8300 committed entries above the follower's snapshot: the feature-on restart never returned within the window (violated, witness index 1), while the same stores restarted without the feature returned (holds, index 3), stayed at the snapshot index (applied_at_snapshot holds, index 3), faced a batch demand (130 expected batches) larger than the capacity observed on that node (replay_exceeds_channel holds, index 3), and left the other two voters with a quorum (holds, index 2). So the stall no longer depends on a non-default batch size, and the stall fact gained this receipt as an execution; the remaining question is only how often ordinary snapshot cadence leaves such a gap.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a CommitTrackingLogStore, NewRaft cannot return when the replay must hand more batches to fsmMutateCh than that channel's 128-slot buffer holds, because the only consumer of the channel is runFSM, which NewRaft starts after the replay returns; the number of batches is ceil(committed-but-unapplied entries / MaxAppendEntries), so 129 entries above the last applied index stall the constructor with MaxAppendEntries 1 and 8193 entries do so with the default 64. Entries that never reach the FSM commit path (LogNoop) are skipped by prepareLog and do not create batches.
knowledge.conditions: Construction of a node whose log store reports a commit index above its snapshot/applied index while the feature is enabled; observed with in-memory stores on harness-supplied stores and on live three-node clusters, the latter both with MaxAppendEntries 1 and 250 entries and with the default 64 and about 8300 entries.

interpretations.rationale: The declared predicate is that a follower restarted with the feature and the default batch size over more committed entries than the FSM mutation channel can hold still finishes NewRaft within the window; the witness contradicts it. Admission index 0 records the live fixture: cluster {A,B,C}, leader B, snapshot index 7, staged commit index 8306, 8299 entries to replay, 130 expected batches at the default MaxAppendEntries 64, and the gap flag true. The feature-on restart at index 1 never returned within 5s; the control restart at index 3 returned as a follower with last_applied 7, i.e. still at the snapshot index, and reported the observed capacity 128 with replay_exceeds_channel true, so the demand exceeded the channel at default settings too. Cluster status at index 2 confirms the other two voters kept a leader. Mechanism: restoreFromCommittedLogs replays through processLogs into fsmMutateCh (api.go 724-754, raft.go 1296-1363) before NewRaft starts the only consumer runFSM (api.go 600-640), and the channel holds 128 batches (api.go 560). Limits: the harness reaches the required gap by configuring a ten-minute SnapshotInterval and taking no snapshot after the early one, which models delayed rather than failed snapshotting, so how often ordinary cadence leaves a gap above 8192 entries is still not established; non-return is observed over a bounded window with permanence argued from source; the stalled constructor is abandoned rather than resumed.
counterevidence: The control restart over the same stores returned and stayed at the snapshot index, so the gap and the stores alone do not explain the stall.
The control event shows the same node observing a 128-slot channel that the fixture's 130 batches exceeded, so the demand really crossed the bound at the default batch size.
limitations: The gap is reached by delayed snapshotting arranged by the harness (ten-minute SnapshotInterval, no further snapshot on that node); no snapshot failure mode is injected.
Non-return is observed over a bounded 5s window; permanence rests on the source argument that no consumer exists before the constructor returns.
In-memory stores and a graceful shutdown; the stalled constructor is abandoned without supervision.

interpretations.rationale: Answer: yes, and no longer only under non-default configuration. A node whose log store reports a commit index that requires more batches than the 128-slot fsmMutateCh buffer cannot finish NewRaft, because the replay runs before the only consumer of that channel is started. Receipts 00386ad8ea534d91a0ef7506fabc9527 (supplied stores, two scales, feature-off controls returning), ea93eea3cc08408ab3cd208ca9b1e5ca (live cluster, MaxAppendEntries 1, 250 entries) and e0d98aadc54b461792883fc8a2a82676 (live cluster, default MaxAppendEntries 64, about 8300 entries, 130 batches against an observed capacity of 128) witness it; the live receipts also show the remaining voters keeping a quorum while the stalled node never starts, so the failure is node-level and does not stop the cluster at that size. Remaining limits: the required gap is reached by delaying snapshots (the harness sets a ten-minute SnapshotInterval and takes no further snapshot), so the frequency with which ordinary snapshot cadence leaves more than 128*MaxAppendEntries committed-but-unapplied entries is unknown - at the default SnapshotThreshold of 8192 the requirement of 8193 entries sits just above the cadence boundary, so a node needs a delayed or failed snapshot to cross it; non-return is observed over a bounded window with permanence argued from source; stores are in-memory, the shutdown graceful and the stalled constructor abandoned without supervision.
counterevidence: Feature-off controls over the identical stores construct normally in every receipt, so the gap and the stores alone do not explain the stall.
No-op entries never reach the FSM commit path and do not stall construction, which scopes the defect to command or barrier entries.
In the live receipts the other voters kept a quorum, so the defect is a node-level startup failure rather than a cluster-wide outage at that size.
limitations: The required gap is produced by delayed snapshotting arranged by the harness rather than by an observed production cadence or a snapshot failure; at default settings the requirement (8193 entries) sits just above the default SnapshotThreshold, so crossing it needs delay or failure.
Non-return is observed over a bounded 5s window in each receipt; permanence rests on the source argument about the missing consumer.
In-memory stores and a graceful shutdown; the stalled constructor is abandoned rather than resumed and no supervision, timeout or restart policy is modelled.
The earlier receipt 2d92d633d32a4a7c9e204b7dc5c8828b remains an identity failure that establishes nothing.
interpretations.joint_history: Four receipts over one question and one mechanism. 2d92d633d32a4a7c9e204b7dc5c8828b is retained as an identity failure (construct events without local_id, no evaluated comparison). 00386ad8ea534d91a0ef7506fabc9527 witnesses the stall on harness-supplied stores at two scales with feature-off controls. ea93eea3cc08408ab3cd208ca9b1e5ca reaches the same stall in a live three-node cluster with MaxAppendEntries 1 and 250 entries; e0d98aadc54b461792883fc8a2a82676 repeats that live scenario with the default MaxAppendEntries 64 and about 8300 entries. They are compatible because the stall condition is the same in each (ceil(replay entries / MaxAppendEntries) exceeds the 128-slot channel) and the live receipts share the same cluster shape, fixture construction and control design; each receipt's comparison outcomes are read from that receipt alone, and the newer receipt's fixture differs in the batch size and gap size it was designed to test.
